searchText: With Sepolia facing issues, attention has quickly moved there for good reasons. With that said, many of us are operating businesses and rely on Holesky for critical day to day development. The updates have become sparse and all over the place, making it hard to understand what is theory and what is reality. I am curious what the latest thinking of Holesky and how those of us running RPC nodes can get nodes back in a decent place. <@552133098075193354> , not sure who else to tag. apologies for the delay, we would be giving a proper update after ACD tomorrow and can do a better job of presenting the current status in the meantime Expect a blog post out in the next 2h or so please let us delay pectra on mainnet - idk where to say this but hoping there's nobody pushing for a fast or rushed release when there have been so many problems not going down is a big part of what makes ethereum valuable Thank you <@199561711278227457> and <@552133098075193354>, will keep an eye out for your updates. Hopefully there is clear direction coming out of this. Pectra **has not** been scheduled on mainnet. Obviously we'll reasses this, figure out a proper testing plan, and only then schedule Pectra. This is why I'm pretty strongly against trying to have "tentative dates" for mainnet upgrades 🙂 I don’t think delaying the mainnet fork accomplishes much. Perhaps it could make time for a shadowfork. I understand why the public is uncertain following two consecutive testnet issues, but I don’t think the problems identified bring any risk to mainnet. A final shadowfork could appease the fear of the public but I don’t think there is another reason to delay. Did anyone manage to get `erigon v2.61.3` working with sepolia? <@552133098075193354> wondering if you all are still tracking to providing an update on Holesky?
